evidence.observation: The row states SI3 'binds the 17 approved ontology deltas out of 414 admitted exports' and that the oracle passed 'for all 34 changed JSON and YAML outputs'. The plan measured a different population and a different scope: 'over the 410 models the Ossie export maps', with the in-scope causes tabulated as 'unit-based reference | 8 | 8' and 'subtype with several supertypes | 5 | 3' (11 models, D3's cost stated as '13 links in 11 models'). 17 is instead the plan's total identification-differs row count, which includes the four out-of-scope objectification rows that §7 excludes and predicate 4 requires to stay. The row totals are also not restated for the larger 414 population, so 'go from 17 to 4' is checked only through the per-class transitions.

concerns.recommendation: Restate the SI3 corpus against the shipped tree: how many ontologies changed, in which models, and the identification-differs totals before and after over the 414 admitted exports. Reconcile the figure 17 with the approved 11-model in-scope corpus, and if the population or scope grew since main f7ee3720, record that growth as a close amendment with the owner's corpus approval rather than as a count in the predicate table.
concerns.title: Predicate 4's corpus figure (17 deltas of 414 exports) matches neither the approved 11-model scope nor the plan's 410-model population

evidence.location: §12 Close amendments, first table row and the closing paragraph
evidence.observation: The approved baseline says of the written flat file that 'given later as an input on its own, has no pins to check, so it gets one named refusal that says to load the root (O2's second branch, for that input only)', and predicate 2 requires that 'a test in which a root or a flat file lists its own elements as included is refused on every route'. §12 replaces that with a conditional diagnostic: 'The named unattended:flat-without-root hint accompanies include-sensitive unattended validation failures' and 'A valid standalone file still loads under its own rules', while the same section closes with 'The approved criteria continue to apply to the final routes.' The affected cells of predicate 1's (route, input) table and predicate 2's fabricated-origin control are not restated, so an otherwise valid standalone file that lists its own elements as included has no recorded expected outcome.

concerns.recommendation: Restate the amended expectations explicitly: which predicate 1 cells for the standalone flat input are now admissions rather than refusals, with their exit codes, and what predicate 2's self-including flat-file control must do under the conditional hint. If the narrowing is an owner-approved criterion change rather than a measurement, record it as a ruling with the digest of the bytes it covers, as §8 requires.
concerns.title: §12 narrows D1's standalone-flat refusal while asserting the approved criteria still apply

evidence.location: 'Phase questions and residuals' table, SI2 timing row
evidence.observation: The sweep records the question as 'The broad local Rmap timing check has exceeded its threshold intermittently' and disposes of it with a single observation: 'The timing node ran in beast-3 shard 3, which exited 0 with 4,175 passing tests. The earlier local fluctuation and its baseline reproduction remain in the SI2 record.' No measured margin against the threshold, no repeat count and no maintenance target are given, in contrast to the same paragraph's treatment of RC-05 and RC-08, which 'retain their prior maintenance targets'.

concerns.recommendation: Record the observed duration against the configured threshold for the beast-3 run (or the number of consecutive green observations), and if the node remains threshold-sensitive on shared hardware, carry it as a named residual maintenance target instead of marking it resolved on one green shard exit.
concerns.title: A known-intermittent timing gate is marked resolved on one green shard run with no margin or residual target

evidence.observation: 'The independent phase reviewer read one digest-bound diff per phase and an SI1 repair-only diff. The review-helper status identifies subsequent repair and release-fold bytes as changed on disk. The phase records and findings ledgers tie the original opinions to those reviewed bytes and list the checks for later repairs.' The checks covering the post-review bytes are the author's own, while plan predicate 6 requires each phase to have 'a record with verbatim gate output and one independent reviewer in a different tool'; close-results repeats that 'The opinions remain on the original brief bytes' without saying which phases' shipped bytes (including the release-note fold 0.5.2 carries) therefore have no independent read.

concerns.recommendation: State per phase whether the bytes that shipped are the bytes the independent reviewer read; where they are not (the release-fold and any post-review repair beyond the SI1 repair-only diff), either obtain an independent read of that diff or record the deviation from predicate 6 explicitly in the close record as owner-visible.
concerns.title: Independent opinions stay on pre-repair bytes and the candidate does not say which shipped bytes lack independent coverage

evidence.observation: 'The milestone requires at least four successful close seats' appears only in the sweep. Plan r2's predicate 6 requires only that 'the close has the light GND panel, a full default lane and a question sweep', §8 records 'Plan and close review: the light GND panel, the owner's choice of 2026-11-25', and §11 mentions a seat count only descriptively for r1 ('four of six seats, every one revise'). concerns.recommendation: Source the four-seat quorum to the governing project rule or record it as an owner decision, and bind the seat accounting (seats dispatched, seats that returned a parseable review, and their dispositions) in the close record so predicate 6's panel gate is checkable against a stated threshold.

summary: Read all three inline artifacts at their stated digests, one pass, no delegation, builds, tests or history. The candidate's predicate mapping is largely coherent (SI2's unchanged 436-model identity digest, the 8-to-0 and 5-to-0 link transitions with four objectification links and two concepts remaining, the remote tag peeling to the merged commit, and a sweep that names residual targets for SI3, SI4 and O8). Four gates are not demonstrably bound to the bytes they claim: the corrected full lane ran on the PR head rather than the merged and tagged tree, with an unnamed two-document diff bridging them; the SI3 figure of 17 approved ontology deltas over 414 admitted exports matches neither the approved 11-model in-scope measurement nor the plan's 410-model population; plan §12 narrows D1's standalone-flat refusal while asserting the approved criteria still apply; and both lanes skip 13 unnamed PyRel tests although predicate 1's table includes both --rules modes. Four hardening items and one completeness item follow.
